It may seem like an obvious answer, but the human eyes and human ears don't see or hear things differently... do they?
Are each human's tongues (and therefore taste) unique?

They would be similar.

To use the example of the eyes, we are not all the same.

colorblindness can result in not seeing part of the 'visible spectrum', and there are some women who actually have an extra protein and can see even more than the normal people. There are typically 3 colour converting proteins.

There are even single nucleotide polymorphisms that can affect the performance of the individual proteins from person to person.

All that said in normal cases what you see is likely in about 99% concordance with your fellows.

It's extremely likely that the sense of taste is just like this. However for your information, tongues don't have a huge variety in tasting capability. taste depends so much more on smell. your tongue can only distinguish five or six different flavors. In concert with your nose, millions.
